scope: Independent audit of the existing 30 profiles. Checked all claimed Singapore RDB3 categories and taxon mappings against the four NParks taxon tables; checked origin in the mammal/bird/amphibian tables and the explicitly introduced frog account. Targeted review of significant biological and fun-fact assertions, not a claim that every sentence or global assessment was independently verified.

summary.remainingNationalEvidenceGap: Kaloula pulchra has no row in the successfully opened NParks amphibian table. Retain the editorial UNV category rather than assigning NA by inference.
genuineErrorsFound: Some profile source cards misidentify BiodiversitySG, Jurong Lake Gardens and an RDB3 table as Flora & Fauna Web.

officialStatusEvidence.note: This table contains no origin column, so its status rows alone cannot establish native origin.

officialStatusEvidence.absence: Kaloula pulchra is absent from the rendered taxon table; it is not a verified RDB3 NA entry.

actionableCorrections.issue: The np() helper hard-codes the source name NParks · Flora & Fauna Web for every URL. Current calls include a BiodiversitySG pangolin page, an NParks RDB3 mammal table and a Jurong Lake Gardens birds page.
actionableCorrections.action: Choose the source name from the verified host/path or make the name an explicit helper argument. Use NParks · BiodiversitySG, NParks · Singapore Red List (RDB3), and NParks · Jurong Lake Gardens for those three cases.

actionableCorrections.classification: unresolved evidence, not an incorrect category

retainExistingSafeguards: RDB3 supersedes RDB2 for the app's national status display. Existing otter, loris, lesser mousedeer, hornbill and junglefowl categories already use the newer column correctly.
Do not transfer the older broad Paradoxurus hermaphroditus global assessment directly to Paradoxurus musangus.
The existing Green turtle note separates dated global Least Concern (2025) from national Critically Endangered. The global DOI was outside this bounded audit.
Introduced occurrence, qualitative encounter frequency, national threat and global threat remain separate concepts.
The 18 global assessment gaps remain explicitly unverified; do not silently mark them reviewed because the national rows were checked.
sourceTableCautionsForNewProfiles: NParks reptile table uses Cuora couro and amphibian table prints Pelobratrachus nasutus and Icthyophis paucisulcus. Check accepted taxon names in a relevant authoritative taxonomic source before blindly reproducing table spellings.
Mammal RDB3 classifies Sambar deer and Dusky langur origin as uncertain with NA, not simply Native.
Mammal RDB3 includes nationally extinct and vagrant animals; do not present them as established present-day residents.
Common myna is listed Native/LC in the current NParks bird table; any conflicting older species-page origin should be documented if that animal is added.
